author: claude-pm
method: Read-only pass over the published native M5 file. Expected grid of 5-minute slots over the note's available interval; a slot-of-week position missing in at least 95 percent of the weeks it occurs in is a fixed closure; a weekday with every open slot missing is a full-day closure; the remainder is grouped into contiguous runs. Scripts: classify_xagusd_gaps.py and break_hours.py beside this record.

counts.fixed_closure_description: Sat 00:00 to Mon 00:00 UTC (576 slots) plus the 23:55 slot on Mon, Tue, Wed and Thu
counts.weekday_run_start_mode_by_month: 23:55 every month except March, 22:55 in March

reading: The missing slots are calendar closures: weekend, a daily break of 60 to 65 minutes beginning at the 23:55 UTC slot (22:55 in March, the daylight-saving month), 21 full-day holidays, and holiday early closes.
587 single-slot gaps over eight years, about 72 a year, are the only candidates for genuine no-tick intervals; none is a multi-hour data hole.
The 2,148 hourly targets without an exact-prior M5 close are the first hour after the daily break; the prior slot was closed, not missing.
The small differences from the note's figures (283,442 and 2,147) come from the interval edge and are immaterial.
ruling_basis: Operator ladder E4568: source first, then weakened treatment, then escalation. The source rung is satisfied for this cell by the data itself; nothing is missing that a broker pull could supply. The weakened label still applies because the period is design-contaminated development, not pristine validation.
limitations: This classifies gaps in the M5 slot grid; it does not inspect prices, spreads or the derived view.
The 95 percent rule is a description of this file; the worker's calendar rule should be explicit per symbol class.
No run, context, precommit or profile was created or changed.
